24238.title: Sketcher: Trim does not work with an external line and a circle
24238.feasibility_reason: The issue describes a specific geometric trim failure involving external lines and circles in the Sketcher workbench. While labeled as a good first issue and confirmed, resolving geometric intersection and trimming logic requires familiarity with CAD kernel interactions (OCC) and the Sketcher's trim tool implementation, which can be non-trivial for an outsider.
blockers: Requires understanding of FreeCAD Sketcher trim algorithm and OCC geometry intersection logic
24238.problem_summary: Sketcher's Trim tool fails when trimming normal sketch geometry (such as a full circle) against external geometry references, deleting the entire geometry rather than trimming it at the intersection point.
24238.root_cause_hypothesis: The intersection calculation in the Sketcher trim algorithm (e.g. within `SketchObject::trim` or the intersection search helper) only tests intersections between normal sketch geometry elements and ignores external geometry (`ExternalGeo` / negative index geometries), causing the algorithm to find no valid cutting intersections and delete the full circle.
24238.suggested_approach: Include external geometry elements when gathering intersecting curves for trimming, calculate the intersection points between the target geometry (the circle) and the external geometry curves, and use these intersection points as valid split/trim boundaries without modifying the external geometry itself.
prerequisites: FreeCAD development environment set up and capable of building the Sketcher module
Understanding of Sketcher's geometry indexing (positive indices for internal sketch geometries, negative indices for external geometries) and OCC intersection algorithms
implementation_steps: Locate the trim intersection calculation routines in `src/Mod/Sketcher/App/SketchObject.cpp` (e.g., methods handling `trim`, `seekIntersectionPoints`, or equivalent).
Inspect how candidate intersecting geometries are collected; identify where external geometries (negative index geometries in `SketchObject::ExternalGeo`) are currently excluded or omitted.
Update the intersection detection logic so that intersections with external geometries are computed using OpenCASCADE intersection algorithms and added to the list of trim cutting points.

Ensure that when the target geometry is split or trimmed, new constraint attachments and vertex creation only modify the sketch's internal geometries and do not attempt to modify the read-only external geometry.
Handle the special case for full circles (converting circle to an arc between intersection points or trimming at the clicked segment).
Add unit/regression tests in `src/Mod/Sketcher/App/SketchObjectTest.py` verifying that trimming a circle against an external line correctly creates an arc bounded by the intersection.

27762.title: Part/PartDesign: General settings page is missing tooltips
27762.feasibility_reason: Adding tooltips to UI widgets in a settings page is a straightforward task involving finding the relevant preference page UI/source files and adding standard tooltips to the controls.
27762.problem_summary: Several widgets and controls on the Part/PartDesign 'General' preferences page in FreeCAD lack descriptive tooltips, making options unclear to users.
27762.root_cause_hypothesis: The Qt Designer UI definition file (.ui) for the Part/PartDesign General preferences page does not have the 'toolTip' property defined for several input widgets and checkboxes.
27762.suggested_approach: Locate the UI file corresponding to the Part/PartDesign General preferences page, identify all controls/checkboxes/inputs lacking tooltips, and add clear, descriptive tooltip text directly in Qt Designer or the .ui XML definition.
prerequisites: Ability to build FreeCAD from source or run a local dev environment with Qt tools
Qt Designer or a text editor to modify Qt .ui XML files
Understanding of Part and PartDesign workbench preferences and their functionality

Inspect the UI file in Qt Designer or XML editor and compare against the settings shown under Edit -> Preferences -> Part/PartDesign -> General.
Draft concise and informative tooltip descriptions for all labels, check boxes, combo boxes, spin boxes, and other controls that currently lack tooltips.
Add the `<property name="toolTip"><string>...</string></property>` entries to the respective widgets in the UI file.
Build and launch FreeCAD, navigate to Edit -> Preferences -> Part/PartDesign -> General, and verify that hovering over every setting widget displays the appropriate tooltip.
Ensure translation strings are properly marked/formatted according to FreeCAD's UI standards and submit a pull request.

19709.title: Measurement: Error when clicking on measure label only on DXF import
19709.feasibility_reason: The issue provides clear reproduction steps and a stack trace indicating a segmentation fault in Gui::SoFCUnifiedSelection::setSelection when clicking a measure label on a DXF import. However, debugging GUI selection handlers and the interaction with imported DXF geometry might require some familiarity with FreeCAD's Inventor/Coin3D integration and selection mechanisms.
19709.problem_summary: FreeCAD crashes with a segmentation fault in Gui::SoFCUnifiedSelection::setSelection when a user clicks on a measurement label in the 3D viewer.
19709.root_cause_hypothesis: When the user clicks on a 3D measurement label, the selection event is handled by SoFCUnifiedSelection. The picked path resolves to an internal measurement Coin node (or an object without a standard document object / selection adapter), and SoFCUnifiedSelection attempts to dereference null or invalid object pointers/metadata when processing the picked element, accompanied by the log 'No measure handler available for geometry of module: Measure'.
19709.suggested_approach: Add null checks and guard against picking non-selectable measurement scene graph nodes in SoFCUnifiedSelection::setSelection and SoFCUnifiedSelection::handleEvent, or ensure measurement label Coin nodes are explicitly marked non-pickable / non-selectable for standard document selection passes.
prerequisites: Build environment for FreeCAD with Coin3D, Qt, and Python bindings enabled.
A test DXF file or generic CAD model reproducing measurement creation in the Measure workbench.
implementation_steps: Reproduce the crash in a debug build by creating a measurement with the Measure tool and clicking directly on the resulting measurement label in the 3D viewport.

Inspect the stack frame in `Gui::SoFCUnifiedSelection::setSelection` and `handleEvent` to identify which pointer dereference or index lookup is causing the SIGSEGV when a measurement label node is picked.
Add null checks and valid-object validation in `SoFCUnifiedSelection` for picked paths that lack a backing `App::DocumentObject` or `Gui::ViewProvider`.
Check measurement Coin nodes (like text / dimension labels in `Mod/Measure`) and verify if their pick style should be set to `SoPickStyle::UNPICKABLE` or handled gracefully if selected.

Investigate and handle the warning 'No measure handler available for geometry of module: Measure' to ensure measurement entities do not recursively attempt to measure themselves or fail silently without crashing.
Test clicking measurement labels across different geometry types (DXF 2D shapes, 3D solids, empty space) to confirm the crash is eliminated and selection behaves as expected.

28930.title: Measurement: Length measured with `Std_Measure` is attached to geometric center, not midpoint
28930.feasibility_reason: The issue clearly identifies the problem and expected behavior in the measurement tool, but locating where the calculation uses the geometric center versus the curve midpoint requires navigating the C++ codebase of the Std_Measure tool.
28930.problem_summary: When measuring the length of a curved edge or spline with Std_Measure, the annotation label/dimension line anchor attaches to the geometric center (barycenter/bounding center) rather than the midpoint lying directly on the curve.
28930.root_cause_hypothesis: The measurement calculation for edge length queries the center of mass (e.g., via `BRepGProp` center of mass or bounding box center) or a similar centroid calculation instead of evaluating the point on the curve at parameter `(u_start + u_end) / 2` or at half of the edge's total arc length.
28930.suggested_approach: Update the point/placement calculation in the measurement code for edge length measurements to evaluate the point at the parametric midpoint or arc-length midpoint of the edge/curve using OpenCASCADE curve evaluation utilities (e.g. `BRepAdaptor_Curve` or `GCPnts_AbscissaPoint`), ensuring the annotation anchor sits directly on the curve.
prerequisites: Build FreeCAD from source with OpenCASCADE (OCC) development headers and Qt support enabled.
implementation_steps: Search the Measure module and Gui measurement commands for the calculation of the position/anchor point for length measurements of TopoDS_Edge and curve objects.
Identify where the barycenter or center of mass is currently computed (such as `GProp_GProps` / `BRepGProp::LinearProperties` or center point computation).

Modify the calculation for edge/curve length measurement to compute the curve's midpoint: retrieve the first and last curve parameters (or use arc length parameterization via `GCPnts_AbscissaPoint`), evaluate the 3D point at the midpoint parameter using OCC's `Value()` or `D0()` method.
Handle edge cases such as closed/periodic curves, zero-length edges, and trimmed curves properly.
Rebuild FreeCAD and verify using Std_Measure on various non-straight curves (splines, circles, arcs, ellipses, complex NURBS edges) to ensure annotations sit on the curve itself.
Run existing measurement unit and GUI tests to ensure no regressions for straight edge length or other measurement types.

30833.title: TechDraw: Keyboard navigation of the Section Plane is chaotic
30833.feasibility_reason: The issue describes a Qt tab-order problem in a TechDraw task panel or dialog. While fixing tab orders in Qt UI files or Python/C++ dialogs is usually straightforward, identifying the exact file and widget hierarchy without prior codebase knowledge may take some investigation.
blockers: Locating the specific UI definition or code responsible for the Section Plane dialog/task panel
30833.problem_summary: Keyboard Tab/Shift-Tab navigation across input fields in TechDraw's Section Plane task panel follows an erratic, non-intuitive sequence.
30833.root_cause_hypothesis: The tab stop order in the Qt UI file (.ui) or programmatic `setTabOrder` chain for the Section Plane task panel widget was not explicitly configured, causing Qt to default to creation order or layout geometry which does not match the visual top-to-bottom / logical input sequence.
30833.suggested_approach: Inspect the Section Plane UI definition file in Qt Designer or code, define an explicit and intuitive tab order (tabstops) linking input fields from top to bottom and left to right, and verify focus behavior during keyboard navigation.
prerequisites: Working FreeCAD development environment with Qt6/Qt5 and Qt Designer
Basic understanding of Qt tab stop ordering and FreeCAD TechDraw TaskPanel architecture
implementation_steps: Locate the UI definition files corresponding to the Section Plane task panel (e.g., TaskSectionView.ui, TaskComplexSection.ui, or related dialog UI files in src/Mod/TechDraw/Gui/).
Open the UI file in Qt Designer and inspect the `<tabstops>` order using the Tab Order editing tool (or check if tab order is set programmatically in the C++ task panel class).
Rearrange the tab stops into a logical top-down, left-to-right sequence covering all interactive controls (spinboxes, line edits, dropdowns, check boxes, and action buttons).
Ensure any dynamic widgets or sub-widgets embedded at runtime maintain proper `QWidget::setTabOrder` relationships.
Build FreeCAD and open the TechDraw workbench.
Launch the Section Plane tool and verify that pressing Tab and Shift-Tab smoothly transitions focus across all fields in the expected sequential order.
Test with other keyboard shortcuts (Enter/Escape) and ensure accessibility remains intact.
